subject: Renewal scope: minimum commit floor and split-invoice options
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@zenhealth.ai>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.inference>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal scope: minimum commit floor and split-invoice options

Rajiv —

Thanks for the time last week. As we prepare the renewal paperwork for ZenHealth (deal ZEN-433), two items came up from your procurement and finance teams that I want to confirm before we finalize the SOW:

1) Minimum commit floor: your finance lead asked whether the annual minimum can be set to a lower floor for the first 6 months (to 60% of the full-year commit) with a hard true-up at month 7. Can you confirm this is what they need, or did they mean a rolling true-up?

2) Split invoicing: you mentioned a desire to split the annual commitment across two invoices (50/50) tied to product milestones (pilot complete / full rollout). That is doable but we need a clear milestone definition in the SOW to automate billing.

Attached is the latest SOW draft (ZenHealth_SOW_v3.pdf) and the usage report through Q3 for context. I want to propose three quick options to accelerate signoff — please indicate which direction you prefer and I’ll generate the contract language:

- Option A (Conservative): Annual commit X with 60% first-half floor, single invoice at start, true-up at month 7.
- Option B (Split + Floor): Annual commit X, 50/50 invoice split by milestone, 60% floor applied pro rata to the first invoice with true-up.
- Option C (Phased Annualize): Start with 6-month committed allocation (50% of annual) at reduced rate, automatic annualize on month 7 to full-year pricing with a rebate if actual usage < committed.

If you want, we can schedule a 20-minute call tomorrow to walk through the numbers.

Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
attachments: ZenHealth_SOW_v3.pdf, usage_report_Q3.csv
From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@zenhealth.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Cc: Marta Alvarez <marta.alvarez@zenhealth.ai>, procurement@zenhealth.ai
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal scope: minimum commit floor and split-invoice options

Ben —

Really appreciate the clear options. Procurement is specifically asking for: a 6-month reduced-floor (60%) with a firm true-up after month 6 (not rolling), and the ability to pay across two invoices tied to customer acceptance of the pilot (invoice 1) and go-live (invoice 2).

Key constraints from our side:
- Finance needs the milestone definitions in the contract (acceptance = 2 weeks of production traffic with <3% error rate).
- We cannot pre-fund more than 60% of the annual commit in the first invoice due to internal cashflow rules.

Can you confirm whether Option B can be implemented with the acceptance criterion above? If so, send a redline we can share with legal.

Thanks,
Rajiv
VP Product & Operations
ZenHealth
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@zenhealth.ai>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.inference>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal scope: minimum commit floor and split-invoice options

Rajiv —

Yes — Option B aligns with your ask and we can incorporate the acceptance definition you provided. I’ve sketched the contract redlines inline below and attached the updated SOW (ZenHealth_SOW_v3.pdf — revised). Highlights:

- Invoice 1 (50%): Due on signature; applied to the first 6-month allocation. We will cap the invoice at 60% of the annual committed units.
- Invoice 2 (50%): Due on milestone (go-live acceptance). If acceptance happens after month 6, Invoice 2 still covers the remaining committed units and triggers the month-7 true-up.
- True-up: A single reconciliation at month 7 comparing actual consumption against the committed annual units. Over-usage billed at standard overage rate; under-usage credited pro rata with the rebate cap as defined in section 4.2.

Three actionable asks for your team so we can produce the legal redline:
1) Confirm the acceptance criterion text ("2 weeks of production traffic with <3% error rate") — are SLA metrics acceptable?
2) Confirm that the finance constraint is strictly that Invoice 1 cannot exceed 60% of annual value.
3) Confirm whether you want the true-up to be cash refund or credit toward next year (we typically offer credit toward next-year invoices for enterprise renewals).

If all good, I’ll ask Legal to publish an updated redline by EOD Wednesday.

Thanks — looping in Priyom (pricing) and Sofia (renewals) to ensure the rebate and billing flows are in scope.

Ben
Director, Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
attachments: ZenHealth_SOW_v3.pdf (rev), usage_report_Q3.csv
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.inference>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal scope: minimum commit floor and split-invoice options

Ben / Priyom —

Forwarding the thread after a quick price check. High-level pricing guidance from Pricing: Option B is fine but we need to lock the rebate cap and the overage multiplier. Proposed parameters:

- Annual commit: 1,200,000 generation tokens (contract units)
- Invoice 1 cap: 60% (720,000 tokens)
- Overage rate: 1.5x standard per-token price for consumption above committed annual units
- Rebate: pro rata credit up to 15% of invoice 1 value if consumption < invoice 1 covered units at month 7 true-up (to limit exposure)

Priyom — can you convert the above into precise contract language and confirm margins with Finance? I want a redline we can hand to Legal that preserves a reasonable PSR and doesn't create a refund liability.

Ben — once Priyom confirms, I’ll share the redline with Rajiv and copy Legal.

Sofia Ivanova
Head of Renewals
Redwood Inference
